conviction_note: No consensus exists (kabuyoho shows no analyst estimate), so the only bar is the company's back-loaded plan (H1 OP 1,100m, FY OP 3,500m, +47.7% on a Mexico recovery). A Q1 print rarely revises anything here, and what I found is a sourced input-cost squeeze already inside that plan, a possible small IEEPA tariff-refund one-off, and mixed domestic auto volumes. These roughly offset to impact_sum -0.05. The scaled number is -0.08 (abs 2.0, p_up 48). The two agree in sign and size, so both are close to an honest zero.
bar: Unsourced as consensus: kabuyoho (https://kabuyoho.jp/reportAnalyst?bcode=3501, 2026-10-08 data) shows no analyst consensus, and no 会社四季報 figure was reachable. Used the company plan from the FY2026/5 決算短信 (https://www.suminoe.co.jp/uploads/2026/07/20260714_202605_4Qtanshin.pdf, 2026-07-14): H1 OP 1,100m yen, FY OP 3,500m. The Q1 bar is set from the company's own progress record: Q1 OP was 454 / 82 / 318m in FY24/25/26, which is 32% / 11% / 36% of the H1 actual, so the implied Q1 OP bar is ~350m. All sizes are capped small because no consensus bar exists.
positioning_check: JPX short register 2026-09-29: 0.0% (no disclosed position >=0.5%), no change. 信用倍率 69.43 (kabutan 2026-10-09), but the margin long is small in absolute terms: about 61k shares on 2026-07-17 (irbank, https://irbank.net/3501/margin), which is about 0.45% of shares and about 5 days of the ~13k-share daily turnover. findings.finding: Petroleum-linked input and energy costs were far above last year through the June-August quarter. Japan's coastal fuel-oil index for Jul-Sep 2026 was 144,100 yen/kl for A heavy oil (+43.2% YoY) and +34.5% YoY for C heavy oil, after the spring Iran-war/Hormuz spike. Suminoe's own July outlook names 中東情勢を発端とした原材料・エネルギー価格の高騰 and plans to pass it on through price revisions 'without delay'. Q1 is the quarter most likely to carry the lag before pass-through.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 prints on estimated dates: 2024-10-11 -1.9% (Q1 OP 82m, a weak start) and 2025-10-14 -2.39% (Q1 OP 318m, which was 47% of the H1 guide). Both Q1 reactions were negative regardless of progress. Estimated-cadence dates only.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The cost spike is public and the company built it into the July plan, which is why this is sized near zero. What is not priced is how much of it Q1 absorbed before price revisions took hold, and with no analyst model nobody has published a Q1 margin estimate. If the market had priced a Q1 squeeze, the stock would be trading below plan-EPS multiples or would have sold off into the print. Instead it sits at 10.7x plan EPS, +0.77% over 20 days and +1.38% over 5.
findings.independence: Company document, same direction: FY2026/5 決算短信 outlook (https://www.suminoe.co.jp/uploads/2026/07/20260714_202605_4Qtanshin.pdf) and FY results slides p.15 (https://suminoe.co.jp/uploads/2026/07/202605_4Qshiryo.pdf) cite raw material and labour cost increases to be passed on. That is a different source, but it is the reason the finding sits inside the guide.

findings.finding: Suminoe said on its 2026-07-30 results call that it temporarily absorbed part of the US tariffs on its North American business and has filed for a refund, but has already expensed part of that amount. CBP's CAPE portal has processed IEEPA refunds since 2026-04-20, paying within 60-90 days of acceptance. A recovery could therefore land in the June-August quarter as a cost reversal or a non-operating gain.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance on this name. In the US run, tariff refunds landed in four names on two days and the reactions split by the direction of guidance, not by the refund.
findings.why_not_priced: Neither the amount nor the timing has been disclosed, and the only mention is one sentence in a call transcript. No wire or analyst has quantified it for this name. It is an inference about timing, which is why it is sized as a fraction of a one-off. If the market had priced it, the call sentence would appear in coverage, and none exists.
findings.independence: CBP process timing from a different source: https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/u-s-customs-and-border-protection-4256388/ (CAPE opened 2026-04-20). That source only establishes that refunds can flow; it says nothing about Suminoe.

findings.finding: The main domestic customer's volumes were mixed across the quarter. Toyota's August 2026 domestic production was 204,487 units (-1.7% YoY) and its overseas production fell 7.6%. Daihatsu's domestic production fell 23.0%. A search snippet (not confirmed in a document) puts Toyota's June domestic production at +14.6%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last year's Q1 domestic auto sales rose 4.7% on firm Toyota volumes, and the stock still fell (estimated -2.39%).
findings.why_not_priced: These are public monthly automaker series, so they are fully priced, and the net direction over June to August is mixed. Sized at zero. Filed because it bears on the quarter.
findings.independence: A holder on the Yahoo board (https://finance.yahoo.co.jp/quote/3501.T/forum, post 2026-09-11) notes '国内の自動車生産 全社減少', which is the same public series read by retail.

outside_window.finding: The FY2027/5 plan needs H2 OP of 2,400m against 1,483m last year, from a Mexico recovery under a new president who was Suminoe Textile de Mexico's CEO. The company has cut its plan at Q3 or year-end in FY25 and FY26. Any plan cut most likely comes at the January or April prints, not at this Q1.

baseline_tension: The findings net to about zero and agree with the baseline's mild negative lean (-0.96, almost all margin_overhang) without adding anything to it. Strongest positive the release could carry: a held plan with Q1 OP at or above ~350m plus a tariff-refund recovery. I looked for returns at prior Q1 prints and found none, so I do not expect a dividend or buyback surprise. Run-up is flat (+0.77% 20d), so nothing is crowded either way.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative resting on a public series): the input-cost finding rests on public fuel-oil data and on a squeeze the company already guided for. Cut from -0.30 to -0.20, and p_up moved from 47 to 48.

Rule 2 (negatives outnumber positives): wrote the strongest positive into baseline_tension and confirmed I had searched for returns and revisions at prior Q1 prints; that left the tariff-refund finding and the zero-sized auto finding unchanged.
